title: Commanders stun Giants in final minute to save their season; what now in NFC East?
author: Charlotte Carroll
content:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — It’s not over yet. The New York Giants had a chance Thursday night to build on their NFC East lead and continue distancing themselves from their closest rivals, but the Washington Commanders spoiled that opportunity with a last-minute comeback, prevailing 24-21 at MetLife Stadium.

After throwing a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions — his first and second of the season — quarterback Jayden Daniels led the Commanders on a three-play touchdown drive that he capped with a 32-yard touchdown strike to Stefon Diggs with less than a minute remaining. Daniels finished his impressive day 23 of 33 for 249 yards and three touchdowns, along with two picks. He also rushed 11 times for 28 yards.

While the Commanders (3-5-1) still have work to do to climb back into the race and catch the 5-3-1 Giants, this was a game they had to have to keep their faint playoff hopes alive. The victory also might take a little heat off coach Dan Quinn after a series of losses and questionable game-management decisions.

The Commanders get to take advantage of a minibye, as they don’t play again until Nov. 23, a “Monday Night Football” game against MVP candidate Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals.

For the Giants, on the other hand, this was a huge missed opportunity. The Commanders had won only once since the beginning of October, and New York had a chance to effectively end Washington’s season. But despite intercepting Daniels twice while nursing a 21-17 lead, the Giants struggled to string together enough drives and were unable to run out the clock. Now, the NFC East looks as if it’s still up for grabs, as a Dallas win Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers would give the Cowboys as many wins (five) as the Giants.

The Athletic Playoff Simulator has the Giants’ playoff odds at 51 percent. The Commanders kept their playoff hopes alive at 13 percent, while the Cowboys’ odds increased to 39 percent. The Cowboys will become the favorites to win the NFC East if they beat the 49ers on Sunday.

Quinn’s job status has become a hot topic in the nation’s capital, and with the minibye upon the Commanders, there would have been a lot of agitation among the fanbase to make a change if Washington had lost Thursday. Even though Quinn led the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game after the 2024 season, the results have gone shockingly in the other direction since.

But the comeback victory Thursday lifted Washington back into the edge of the NFC East race. The Commanders are just two games back of the division-leading Giants, and they own the edge over New York, whom they beat and tied.

At this point in Quinn’s career, optics matter. The sense at team headquarters in Ashburn, Va., is that Commanders leadership would rather not make a coaching change midseason. But Quinn and his team can’t make any more game-management gaffes.

Quinn avoided another snafu in the fourth quarter when he challenged a ruling that Giants quarterback Jameis Winston had gained enough for a first down on a third-and-short quarterback sneak. The play was overturned, which gave the Commanders late hope — finally, a key game-management decision finally going in Quinn’s favor. — Barry Svrluga, senior writer

Pretty darn good. Daniels is the future of the franchise and the only reason Washington is playing four primetime games in a five-game stretch. Though the offensive system and play calling of first-year offensive coordinator David Blough is still having some hiccups, Daniels is showing why he’s the centerpiece of the entire Commanders operation.

On Thursday night, he bounced back from a pair of bad interceptions to deliver the game-winning 32-yard touchdown pass to Diggs with 57 seconds remaining.

You can’t totally ignore those interceptions, largely because both came at inopportune times. Yet Daniels was dynamic. He ran the ball effectively, his accuracy continues to impress, and he’s finding a way to move the ball without Terry McLaurin, his top receiver, who’s out for the season. — Svrluga

Didn’t see this one coming but … Ben Sinnott? The 2024 second-round pick entered this game with only one catch for 6 yards this season and hadn’t totaled more than 36 receiving yards in a game in his career (he got that off one catch against the Giants last December). For the past few seasons, the production from the Commanders’ tight ends has come courtesy of two players: Zach Ertz in 2024 and ’25, and Chig Okonkwo this season.

But Sinnott finally showed more of what he’s capable of in the pass game, catching four passes for 42 yards, including a 1-yard touchdown at the end of the first half. He also hurdled a defender on a 12-yard catch and caught a 24-yarder that helped set up Antonio Williams’ 31-yard score in the third quarter. — Nicki Jhabvala, Commanders beat writer

The Giants blew a golden opportunity to take a commanding lead in the NFC East. They’re still in good shape with a 5-3-1 record, but now the 3-5-1 Commanders are right on their tails and hold the tiebreaker. The 4-5 Cowboys also remain in striking distance. A win Thursday night certainly would have made things more comfortable for New York.

A couple of weeks ago, coach John Harbaugh called the Giants’ two divisional games coming out of the bye the most pivotal of the season so far. While the Giants took care of Philadelphia in Week 9, they missed the opportunity to go 2-for-2 and deliver a knockout blow to another NFC East rival. Now the Giants face a daunting stretch with games against some of the best teams in the NFL. It starts next week against one of the best teams in the AFC, the Jacksonville Jaguars. Then, after a visit to Indianapolis to take on the lowly Colts, the Giants must battle two of the NFC’s best in the 49ers and the Seattle Seahawks. — Dan Duggan, Giants beat writer

McCarthy hasn’t backed down from a daunting challenge. Despite being in New York for only about six weeks, his understanding of the offense is excellent. And somehow, someway, he almost always seems to place the ball where it needs to be.

Now, he couldn’t lead the Giants on a tying or game-winning drive at the end of regulation — he ended up, on a desperation third-down heave, throwing his first interception since his New York debut against New Orleans — but that’s not enough to call this game a disappointment, at least individually.

There was no better example of McCarthy’s poise than on his 66-yard, fourth-quarter touchdown throw to tight end Isaiah Likely. The 23-year-old QB delivered a strike with pressure in his face on a crucial third down. The score gave the Giants a 21-17 lead that New York let slip through its grasp. McCarthy finished the night 23-of-36 passing for 293 yards. He also rushed six times for 34 yards, showing off that dynamism that got him into the starting lineup in the first place. Give him credit, too, for bouncing back from a hip injury Sunday to get ready to play on short rest. — Charlotte Carroll, Giants beat writer

Much ado was made about the Giants’ attempts to upgrade at running back ahead of the trade deadline, including reported interest in the Colts’ and Falcons’ stars. The Giants ended up standing pat at the deadline, however, entrusting their backfield to Cam Skattebo, who arrived Thursday at MetLife Stadium in a Giants-themed “Iron Man” helmet.

It was a bold choice for the running back, who missed last weekend’s win in Philadelphia with a lingering hamstring injury. But that’s Skattebo. He’s been nothing but bold in his young career. While he heard the trade chatter about players his team pursued, he clearly didn’t let it bother him enough to affect his performance. In fact, coming off his first career 100-yard game against the Houston Texans in Week 7, Skattebo delivered another sterling performance, rushing for 78 yards and two touchdowns on 18 carries. He also came up clutch a couple of times in pass protection, helping keep McCarthy clean in the pocket. That all added up to a superhero-esque showing for the young running back. — Carroll
